subject: Dedicated capacity: constraints, success metrics, and rollout path
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan@auroraai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: constraints, success metrics, and rollout path

Evan — thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

What you told us (primary pain points)
- Production latency variability during daytime peaks causes poor UX for search/autocomplete features.
- Cost unpredictability from bursty cloud endpoints; finance wants a predictable monthly unit cost for embedding + chat traffic.
- Regulatory requirement: model inference must be run in a logically isolated environment (no multitenant compute for core customer data).

Current stack and usage signals
- Currently on public LLM endpoints (various providers) with autoscaling groups in GCP.
- Peak observed: ~420 TPS sustained for 10–15 minute windows during regional peak; typical baseline ~70–90 TPS.
- Typical prompt length ~140 tokens, average response 220 tokens.

Success criteria (what Aurora needs to sign off)
- Predictable cost: committed capacity with <10% monthly overage variance vs commit.
- Latency: p95 tail < 250 ms for short-turn features (search) and p95 < 600 ms for chat flows at sustained 400 TPS.
- Isolation: customer-dedicated GPU pools with logical networking separation + documented KMS integration.
- Operational: 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated pool, rollout plan that supports canary and fast rollback.

Preliminary fit assessment (Redwood view)
- Dedicated reserved GPU pools are a strong match for predictable TPS and isolation requirements.
- Autoscaling/burst: Recommend a reserved baseline sized for sustained 450 TPS with burst capacity via short-term burst tokens to 650 TPS for 5–10 minute windows. This keeps unit economics predictable while covering observed spikes.
- Cache and batching: We can configure prefix caching for frequent queries and continuous batching windows to drive down per-token cost without harming p95 targets.

Open technical questions we need from Aurora to finalize sizing
1) Which model family(s) do you plan to serve on Dedicated (open weights or managed?) — we need model footprints to finalize GPU count.
2) Do you require physical (single-tenant) hardware or is logical/dedicated GPU pools with strict tenancy controls sufficient?
3) Expected audit window for logs / retention policy (required for SOC/compliance worksheet).

Attachments: capacity-template.xlsx (please fill token distribution + seq length histograms), SLA-draft.pdf (initial draft for dedicated SLA).

Next steps (agreed on call)
- Evan: share the token histogram export and preferred model families by Fri, Apr 23.
- Mina/Rishi: schedule a 60-min capacity-sizing + SRE call for week of Apr 26.
- Marissa: prepare committed pricing sketch and procurement timeline to sync with Aurora procurement.

If that all looks right I’ll create a short mutual action plan and share HubSpot + Doc links. Happy to hop on a brief follow-up if anything above needs correction.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Senior AE, Dedicated & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
M: +1 (415) 555-0147

[attachment: capacity-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)] [attachment: SLA-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Evan Brooks <evan@auroraai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aurora AI Procurement <procurement@auroraai.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 17:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: constraints, success metrics, and rollout path

Mina — thanks for the clear write-up. Confirming and adding color:

- Correct on observed peaks — our monitoring shows 380–450 TPS as the 95th percentile peak in the US region, with rare bursts to ~600 TPS for under 10 minutes.
- Model families: primarily open encoder-decoder variants (we're evaluating Llama2-variants and a 70B family). We'll send the exact model names/weights.
- Isolation: logical/dedicated GPU pools with strict tenancy controls + VPC peering is acceptable; physical single-tenant only if price delta is < 30%.
- Logs: 90-day retention minimum for request/response metadata; 1yr for audit logs (we can discuss retention tiers).

Procurement timeline: Aurora Finance wants a vendor contract signed by end of May; procurement will need committed pricing and an initial 6–9 month reserved capacity proposal. Procurement contact will circulate an initial vendor checklist — copying them now.

I will: share the token histogram export and a short response about model family choices by Thu, Apr 23.

One ask for Rishi/engineering: can you include a brief note about degradation policies (what Redwood recommends if the pool hits sustained >750 TPS)? We want to understand graceful degradation options.

— Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Product, Aurora AI

Cc:
Date: Sun, 19 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: constraints, success metrics, and rollout path

Looping in a couple of technical asks before the sizing call:

- Please ask Aurora for model checkpoints (exact names + quantization tolerance). If they plan to load multiple model families concurrently we need per-model memory and peak KV cache figures.
- I'll prepare two capacity sketches: (A) baseline reserved for 450 TPS sustained, (B) conservative reserved for 600 TPS sustained with burst headroom. Each sketch will include GPU count, expected p95 latency estimates, and estimated monthly cost.
- Degradation policy: short note — recommend staged fallback: prefix cache > reduced kv cache size > lower precision variant > model variant fallback > graceful 429s with user-facing messaging. I'll put this into the sizing doc and link a JIRA ticket.

I'll create JIRA CAP-3121 and attach the sizing sketches + degradation policy. Mina: can you confirm the preferred SRE contact from Aurora so we can invite them to the call?

Thanks,
Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
